about: The priest prays this portion of the Canon quietly, in communion with the Church. This form recalls the Holy Spirit’s appearance to the Apostles and is used from the Pentecost Vigil through the Saturday of its octave. After commemorating the saints, he asks the Father for His protection through Christ.

alignments.gloss: celebrate the most sacred day of Pentecost
appeared to the Apostles in countless tongues

s01.translation: We are in communion and celebrate the most sacred day of Pentecost, on which the Holy Spirit appeared to the Apostles in countless tongues,

s02.translation: and we also venerate the memory, first of all, of the glorious ever-Virgin

s04.translation: Mary, Mother of God and our Lord

s07.translation: and also of blessed Joseph, Spouse of the same Virgin,

alignments.gloss: of Your blessed Apostles and Martyrs

s08.translation: and of Your blessed Apostles and Martyrs: Peter and Paul, Andrew, James, John, Thomas, James, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Simon and Thaddeus;

s09.translation: Linus, Cletus, Clement, Sixtus, Cornelius, Cyprian, Lawrence, Chrysogonus, John and Paul, Cosmas and Damian;

alignments.gloss: we may be defended by the help of Your protection

s10.translation: and of all Your saints. Through their merits and prayers, grant that in all things we may be defended by the help of Your protection.

s12.translation: Through the same Christ, our Lord. Amen.

w001.explanation: The communion of the praying Church includes the commemoration of Mary and the saints whose names follow in this prayer.

w006.explanation: The Apostles receive the Holy Spirit’s manifestation. The phrase about countless tongues describes the manner of that appearance.

w017.explanation: The memorial includes Mary, Joseph, the named Apostles and Martyrs, and all the saints. Their merits and prayers are invoked in the petition for God’s protection.
